body: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) said on October 26, 2026, that it had arrested two men accused of preparing close-range drone attacks from inside Russia. The alleged targets included part of Moscow's missile defense system and a power facility, and the drones were to be remotely operated from Ukraine, according to the FSB. The agency accused the two men of working for Ukraine's security service, saying they collected first-person-view drones and explosive components from hidden locations in the Smolensk and Kaluga regions, assembled them, transported them to the Moscow region, and launched them before handing control to operators in Ukraine.

Russian authorities said the two suspects are from the South Caucasus, born in 1991 and 1998, but did not release their nationalities or names. The men were remanded in custody on terrorism-related charges. Russia did not disclose the specific targets or explain how the drones would be operated from Ukraine, and released video reportedly includes confessions and footage of the drones being assembled and prepared.

The case comes amid repeated drone-related disruption around Moscow. On October 23, 2026, four airports serving Moscow suspended arrivals and departures simultaneously as Russian air defenses intercepted incoming drones, the second simultaneous closure in two days. The airports were Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo, and Zhukovsky, and Sheremetyevo guided passengers to shelter, including passengers on parked aircraft. The article also notes Russia's expanding use of jet-powered Shahed attack drones: Ukraine's Air Force said a Russian attack on the night of October 9-10 involved 160 drones, including 110 jet-powered Shaheds, of which 117 were shot down or jammed, including 82 jet-powered models, with strikes recorded at 14 locations.
en.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service says it arrested two men on October 26 accused of preparing close-range drone attacks from inside Russia against part of Moscow's missile defenses and a power facility, with the drones to be operated remotely from Ukraine.
en.title: Russia says it foiled close-range drone attack on Moscow missile defenses

body: 俄羅斯聯邦安全局表示，於2026年10月26日逮捕兩名男子，指控兩人正從俄羅斯境內準備近距離無人機攻擊。據俄方說法，攻擊目標包括莫斯科飛彈防禦系統的一部分與一處電力設施，無人機預計由烏克蘭遠端操控。俄方指控兩人為烏克蘭安全局工作，並從斯摩棱斯克與卡盧加地區的隱藏地點取得第一人稱視角無人機與爆裂物零件，依指示組裝、運往莫斯科地區並啟動，再交由烏克蘭境內操作人員接管。
俄羅斯當局稱兩名嫌犯來自南高加索，分別出生於1991年與1998年，但未公布國籍與姓名；兩人因涉恐怖主義相關罪名被羈押候審。俄方未公布具體目標，也未說明無人機如何從烏克蘭操控；俄方公布的影片據報包含嫌犯自白與疑似組裝、準備無人機的畫面。

此案發生之際，莫斯科周邊空中交通近期多次因無人機攻擊受擾。2026年10月23日，服務莫斯科的四座機場同時暫停起降，俄方防空系統攔截來襲無人機，這是兩天內第二次同時關閉；受影響機場包括謝列梅捷沃、多莫傑多沃、伏努科沃與茹科夫斯基，謝列梅捷沃並將旅客引導至掩蔽處，包括停在停機坪飛機上的旅客。文章另指出，俄羅斯擴大使用噴射動力沙赫德攻擊無人機；烏克蘭空軍稱2026年10月9日至10日夜間的俄羅斯攻擊共出動160架無人機，包括110架噴射動力沙赫德，至清晨共擊落或干擾117架，包括82架噴射動力機型，並在14處地點記錄到打擊。
